title: Add a .gitignore and README.md
description: Set up project hygiene for `hcc-git-practice` by ignoring sensitive and temporary files, and writing a formatted project README.
steps: Create a test file `app.log` and `.env` — run `git status` and verify Git completely ignores them
Create or update `README.md` with: a title `# HCC Git Practice`, a short description, `## Features` list, and a bash code block showing `git status`
Commit: `git commit -m "chore: add .gitignore and project README"`
expected_output: Git status shows only `.gitignore` and `README.md` tracked; `*.log` and `.env` are invisible to Git.
tips: Filenames starting with a dot like `.gitignore` are hidden files on Unix/macOS and Windows.
To un-track a file that was previously committed by mistake: `git rm --cached <file>`.
